claims.text: In situ high-resolution TEM with an integrated heating stage can capture atomic rearrangements and phase transitions in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at elevated temperatures.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial nanoparticles have a random solid-solution structure at room temperature.
Controlled heating can be applied during HR-TEM imaging using an in situ heating holder.
The experiment is conducted under high vacuum with stepwise temperature increases and real-time atomic-resolution imaging.
Elevated temperature causes atomic diffusion and rearrangement in the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The atomic rearrangement is mediated by thermodynamically driven phase transformations.
Thermal energy increases atomic mobility within the nanoparticles.
Increased atomic mobility can produce changes in local ordering.
Heating may cause phase precipitation or other phase-transition phenomena in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
HR-TEM can resolve the proposed thermally induced phenomena at the atomic scale.
Heating will produce observable atomic rearrangements, lattice-parameter changes, phase boundaries, or nucleation of new phases.
The observed structural changes will correlate directly with increasing temperature.
At room temperature, the nanoparticles exhibit a nearly uniform random solid solution without notable phase separation.
Electron-beam effects and deviations from ideal vacuum conditions may influence the observations.
SAED patterns and quantitative interatomic-distance measurements can be used to monitor structural changes during heating.
